Thanks for the review!

Another question: MDB is master-slave based, and the answer from the slave has no information about the master command that triggered it. I tried to solve this with conversations, but in the current state, you still need to click on the request first to have the response dissected correctly, because it is using the last command encountered as the base to decode the answer. Is there a better way to do that?
That is wrong, you cannot depend on the order of access to the packets when dissecting them. Have a look at request-response tracking in the documentation on how to handle this.
I tend to write these by maintaining a table on the first pass, and write to a separate table (or even per-packet info) to store the result, which is then just looked up when already 'visited'.

Also, see the warnings at the end of Clang + Code checks in the pipeline (https://gitlab.com/chrysh/wireshark/-/jobs/7451216194).

i.e.,
Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-mdb.c:884 proto_tree_add_item called for hf_mdb_bv_bill_enable  -  item type is FT_UINT8 but call has len 2

Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-mdb.c:886 proto_tree_add_item called for hf_mdb_bv_bill_escrow_enable  -  item type is FT_UINT8 but call has len 2

and

@martin.r.mathieson Can you tell be a dissector where you have used such a table, as inspiration?

I would recommend reading section 2.2 in doc/README.dissector, even if you don't end up using the actual conversation mechanism - it should motivate the need to store info on the first pass, then access what you need for when frames are dissected again later (which could include information that is not available at all on the first pass).

These might not be the best examples, but I'll try.

If you are able to look up a normal conversation for your type (looks like this might not be true for you) you can follow a pattern like in packet-udpcp.c

So udpcp_conversation_t is a struct used to maintain the state for one 'conversation' during the first pass.  Later passes consult the conversation to try to link between data requests and acknowledgements.  Note that this (simple) approach wouldn't work if sequence numbers ever wrapped around..

Another approach is to maintain a 'result table' that gets filled in on the first pass and then read on later passes.  The key to this can be (or include) the frame number (pinfo->num).

If you can't use the normal conversation mechanism to group together related frame info, you could just maintain your own tables with whatever keys make sense.  packet-mac-lte.c maintains separate GHashTables for building up a picture during the first pass then storing the result for displaying on later passes.  e.g.,

This word is taken from the MDB standard:

110: MANUAL DISPENSE

Note: These responses can only be sent if the Bill Recycler expansion commands are enabled by the VMC (b1=1) and the VMC has request the RECYCLER ENABLE (37 04) command.
I believe he is saying it should be "dispense" and not "despense."
Thanks

This is a bad assumption (that request will be in previous frame)! What if there were some frames for a different conversation here, or a frame that wasn't even MDB?

Maybe a better design would be to have in mdb_conversation_info_t only the most recent cmd (maybe along with request-framenum + request-timestmp, and only consult it on the first pass (!visited())
But then remember for each frame  remember what you need to (e.g. cmd type, request frame, time delta)?

If you just had a single table whose key was frame number, you could store what it needs to know, e.g. for a response the cmd.

This will never work correctly. 

You cannot assume sequential access to the packets. Therefore last_cmd can become anything depending on which packet to select in the GUI.

To address this use request-response tracking, as described in the corresponding README file. An attempt is made around lines 430-450, but this is not good enough. The assumption used there cannot hold either.
